title: Level-order traversal with a queue
summary: Visit a tree level by level. A queue remembers which nodes are waiting.

checkpoints.text: The tree has three levels. The queue starts with one entry, which points at the root, 40.
40 left the queue and is printed. Its children, 20 and 60, will join at the rear.
20 is printed. 60 is still waiting in the queue, and 20's children, 10 and 30, will join behind it. A level only starts after the whole level above it.
60 is printed before 10 and 30, because it joined the queue before them. 10 and 30 are waiting now.
40 20 60 10 30 50: level by level, left to right. Searching a graph breadth-first (BFS) works the same way, with the same queue.
